Traced installed sqlglot (not executed). parser.py:7633-7636: a quoted function-name token (TokenType.IDENTIFIER) becomes exp.Anonymous(this=Identifier(quoted=True)). generator.py:4204-4210 anonymous_sql calls self.func(self.sql(expression,'this'), ...) so the name is already rendered with quotes ("quote_ident"); func() (4941) calls normalize_func, which at 1126-1128 does name.upper() when normalize_functions is 'upper'/True, the documented default (generator.py:118-119). RlsGuardRunner rewrites the SQL (rls.py:335, tree.sql(..., normalize_functions=False)), then when rules are active calls _refuse_denied_functions(rewritten, dialect) (safety/__init__.py:196-197), which calls assert_no_denied_functions (readonly.py:590-604). That parses the rewritten SQL, walks every node and calls _refuse_denied_function (readonly.py:579-587). For an exp.Anonymous node the candidate is node.name.lower() (readonly.py:489-490). A quoted "pg_sleep"(1) is parsed by sqlglot as Anonymous with the unquoted text pg_sleep, matching the postgres denylist entry "pg_sleep" (readonly.py:379). The check raises UnsafeSqlError, and the test at tests/unit/test_rls_views.py:765 covers this case. Limits: I could not execute the code, and sqlglot's source was not available in the views. The sqlglot behaviour (quoted identifier followed by a paren becomes Anonymous with the bare name) is from my knowledge, not a read. The rewrite and the guard are also traced by reading only. Even if the quoted form failed to parse, _parse_statements would still raise UnsafeSqlError (readonly.py:575-576), but the test's message match would then differ.

tests/unit/test_safety_rls.py:240 comment says SQLite names an unaliased result column after the call's text. SQLite's documented/known behaviour (short_column_names off, default column name for an expression is the original expression text span) matches; so the written case of printf is visible in the column name and the case-preserving test is meaningful. The comment does not claim more. I did not execute sqlite3.
